structure.organization: By consultation category and formula type

consultation_patterns.which-god: Asking which deity to approach for specific needs
consultation_patterns.concerning-X: General inquiry about a topic (τί χρή formula)

historical_context.oracle_function: Zeus's oracle at Dodona, one of Greece's oldest oracles
historical_context.social_evidence: Shows concerns of ancient Greeks across social classes
historical_context.linguistic_evidence: Preserves various Greek dialects (Doric, Ionic, etc.)

translation.greek: τίνι θεῶν εὔχομαι περὶ οἰκίας καὶ σωτηρίας;
translation.english: To which of the gods should I pray concerning my household and safety?
translation.note: εὔχομαι in oracular petitions commonly means “pray” (often with the nuance of making a vow). The possessive with οἰκία (‘household’) is understood though not expressed. σωτηρία denotes physical safety/preservation rather than theological ‘salvation.’ The phrase τίνι θεῶν uses a partitive genitive, ‘which (one) of the gods.’

context.original_paraphrase: To which of the gods should I pray (make vows) concerning my household and safety?
context.notes: Private query; Thessalian features in the tablet. Good general-purpose template.

translation.greek: ἡ πόλις ἐπερωτᾷ περὶ τοῦ σημεῖου· τί λώϊον καὶ ἄμεινον;
translation.english: The city inquires concerning the portent: what is better and more advantageous?
translation.note: σημεῖον = ‘sign, portent,’ i.e., an omen attributed to Zeus; the query seeks guidance on its import. τί λώϊον καὶ ἄμεινον is a Dodonaic formula (‘what is better and more advantageous?’), with λώϊον (epic/poetic comparative) roughly synonymous with ἄμεινον; an implicit ‘course of action’ is understood.

context.original_paraphrase: The city asks about the sign that appeared: what course is better and more advantageous?
context.notes: Public query; Doric. Useable as an omen-interpretation template.

translation.greek: τίνι θεῶν θύω καὶ εὔχομαι ἵνα εὖ πράξω;
translation.english: To which of the gods am I to sacrifice and pray, in order that I may prosper?
translation.note: θύω denotes offering (typically animal) sacrifice; εὔχομαι here has the cultic sense “to pray.” The idiom εὖ πράξω means “to prosper, fare well.” The construction ἵνα + subjunctive (πράξω) expresses purpose. The present indicative in this consultative question (“am I to…?”) is common in Dodona queries.

context.original_paraphrase: To which god should I sacrifice and pray so that I may succeed?
context.notes: Doric; pairs well with success/enterprise questions.

translation.greek: περὶ σωτηρίας παιδὸς καὶ γυναικός· τί χρὴ ποιεῖν;
translation.english: Concerning the safety of the child and the wife: what should be done?
translation.note: σωτηρία denotes safety/preservation; I render it as “safety.” The possessive (“my”) is understood from context but not expressed. τί χρὴ ποιεῖν is the stereotyped Dodona formula, literally “what is it necessary to do?”, here translated idiomatically as “what should be done?”.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning the welfare/safety of his child and wife: what should be done?
context.notes: Laconic but clear theme; good as topic lamella.

translation.english: Concerning the lawsuit: what should be done?
translation.note: δίκη here means a legal case/lawsuit rather than abstract ‘justice’; τί χρή is an abbreviated oracular formula for τί χρὴ (ποιεῖν), ‘what should [one] do?’

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning the legal dispute: what should be done?
context.notes: Very short tablet; use as a legal-topic lamella.

translation.greek: περὶ πορείας· ἆρ’ ἀσφαλές; τί λώϊον;
translation.english: Concerning a journey: is it safe? What is preferable?
translation.note: πορεία means ‘journey/travel’ (also ‘march’ in military contexts). ἆρα marks a yes/no question; ἀσφαλές is the neuter predicate ‘safe.’ τί λώϊον employs the comparative λώϊος ‘better, preferable,’ with an ellipsis of the understood course of action (‘to do’), a typical Dodona brevity.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning travel: is it safe? What is the better course?
context.notes: Good generic travel query; pairs with ‘better/advantageous’ formula.

translation.greek: περὶ γενεᾶς· τίνι θεῶν εὔχομαι ἢ θύω ἵνα τέκνα γένηται;
translation.english: Concerning progeny: To which of the gods should I pray or offer sacrifice, so that children may be born?
translation.note: περὶ γενεᾶς functions as a topic heading (“concerning offspring/lineage”). τίνι θεῶν combines the dative of the verb with a partitive genitive (“which of the gods”). εὔχομαι here = “pray” (cultic), and θύω = “offer sacrifice.” ἵνα τέκνα γένηται expresses purpose; the subject and beneficiary (“to me/us”) are understood.

context.original_paraphrase: About having descendants: to which god shall I pray or offer so that children may be born?
context.notes: Female participle in the tablet; clean template.

translation.greek: περὶ πραγματείας· τί λώϊον καὶ ἄμεινον;
translation.english: Concerning a business undertaking: what is more advantageous and better?
translation.note: πραγματεία has a broad range (“affair, occupation, enterprise;” sometimes even “lawsuit”); in Dodona dossiers it often denotes trade or a business venture, hence the rendering “business undertaking.” λώϊον (epic form, with diaeresis) means “more advantageous/preferable,” and its pairing with ἄμεινον (“better”) is a formulaic pleonasm in oracular questions; the object (“what [course of action]”) is understood elliptically.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning business/enterprise: what is better and more advantageous?
context.notes: Use category as topic lamella; page content pending on DOL.

translation.english: Concerning property: what ought to be done?
translation.note: τί χρή is an elliptical oracular formula for “what ought [to be done]?”, with impersonal χρή (‘it is necessary/one ought’); κτήματα denotes possessions or estate.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning possessions/property: what should be done?

translation.greek: περὶ ἀφέσεως δούλου· τί λώϊον καὶ ἄμεινον;
translation.english: Concerning the manumission of a slave: what is better and more advantageous?
translation.note: ἀφέσεως: legal term for the release/manumission of a slave; at Dodona typically refers to freeing a slave by dedication to the god. τί λώϊον καὶ ἄμεινον: a standard oracular formula asking for the preferable course (‘which is better and more advantageous?’), elliptical for ‘what should one do?’.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning manumission: what is better and more advantageous?

translation.greek: περὶ ἀφέσεως ἢ κρίσεως· τί χρή;
translation.english: Concerning release or adjudication: what is to be done?
translation.note: ἀφέσις here likely means abandoning/remitting a legal claim (i.e., dropping the suit), contrasted with κρίσις “judgment/adjudication, trial.” τί χρὴ is elliptic for “what should (I/we) do?” in oracular queries.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning manumission or a ruling about freeing a slave: what should be done?

translation.greek: περὶ τῶν καρπῶν· ἦ ἂν ἐντελεῖς γένοιντο;
translation.english: Concerning the crops: would they turn out complete?
translation.note: ἐντελεῖς (“complete, entire”) here likely conveys “full/abundant” with reference to the yield; γένοιντο is the potential optative (“would they become/turn out”), with ἦ ἄν marking a question about the prospective outcome. “Crops” renders καρποί in its agricultural sense.

context.original_paraphrase: About the crops the earth bears: will they come to full fruition?
context.notes: Clear yes/no outcome form; Ionian features.

translation.english: Concerning repayment/fulfilment: what should be done?
translation.note: ἀποδοσέως/πληρωμῆς presents alternative or variant terms; both denote “payment/fulfilment,” often of a vow or other obligation. τί χρή is a standard oracular formula meaning “what is necessary/what should be done?”

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning a payment: what should be done?

translation.english: or belonging to another and not this one?
translation.note: ἀλλότριον (neut.) means “belonging to another; someone else’s,” used substantively. The feminine demonstrative τήνδε (“this [one]”) presupposes a feminine noun understood from the context (e.g., γυνή “woman/wife”). The gender mismatch suggests ellipsis typical of Dodona queries; some editors emend to ἀλλοτρίαν to agree with an implied feminine referent. The line is the second alternative in a binary question.

context.original_paraphrase: Or one belonging to another, and not this one? (supplementary)
context.notes: Pairs with 2432 answer; tree/temenos ritual context.

translation.note: The line consists only of an em dash, which in editorial practice typically marks a lacuna or illegible/missing text; there is no Greek to translate. Without further context from the tablet or edition, the content cannot be restored.

context.original_paraphrase: Answer prescribing: set apart the wild olive; offer pure flour to the hero (seasonal rites).
context.notes: Use as sample of Dodona-style oracular *answer*; pairs with 2430.

translation.note: αἶ is a Northwest Greek/Doric yes–no interrogative particle (cf. Attic ἆρα). νικήσω is formally ambiguous between future indicative and aorist subjunctive; in oracle questions it is best taken as future indicative. δίκη here means ‘lawsuit, legal case,’ not abstract ‘justice.’

context.notes: Doric future form νικασέω on tablet; normalize to common νικήσω for skeleton.

translation.greek: περὶ τοῦ σώματος· τί ποιήσας/ποιήσω ὑγιαίνω;
translation.english: Concerning my body: what should I do to be in good health?
translation.note: The transmitted text has a variant ποιήσας/ποιήσω: either an aorist participle (‘having done [what]’) or a deliberative aorist subjunctive (‘what should I do?’). In both, a purpose relation to ὑγιαίνω (‘be in good health’) is understood, with ἵνα/ὅπως often omitted in Dodona formulae; the present ὑγιαίνω carries the sense ‘so that I may be healthy.’ περὶ τοῦ σώματος is the standard rubric ‘about [my] body/health.’

context.original_paraphrase: About the body: what should I do to become healthy?
context.notes: Late 4th c.; perfect for practical counsel queries.

translation.english: Concerning health: what is to be done?
translation.note: τί χρή is a formulaic oracular inquiry using the impersonal χρή (“it is necessary/required”), with an implied infinitive such as ποιεῖν; hence the sense is “what should be done?” (often understood as “what should I do?”). The subject is unspecified.

context.original_paraphrase: Concerning health: what should be done?
